statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk of 12% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold.
recommendation: Conditions are described as normal and two-sided. The narrow flagged window runs from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC (15:30-17:00 Berlin), covering the U.S. cash open and the Richmond Fed / Fed-speaker cluster. Stress is moderate rather than low, so wider-than-usual intraday ranges are plausible without the persistent no-retracement path that defines the tail case.
headline: Record Nasdaq close gives way to a flat, fully retraced overnight tape
body: Nasdaq-100 cash closed Monday at 30,482.35, up 2.83% and a record close, led by AI and semiconductor strength, a 3.4% fall in Brent crude and softer Treasury yields. Overnight the front NQ contract has held a narrow, two-sided range and sits near 30,805, only 0.06% above the 30,784.75 prior settle, with S&P 500 futures essentially unchanged and VIX at 14.87. Quote feeds disagree on the exact overnight extremes, so no session-extreme structure is claimed here. Tokyo is closed for a public holiday, so Asian volume is light. The 10-year yield eased to about 4.96% after last week's Federal Reserve hike to 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase since 2023. Observed mean reversion, low implied volatility and the absence of one-way structure keep Tail in the low band. Stress stays moderate because the coming session carries a dense catalyst stack: the U.S. cash open, the Richmond Fed index and two Fed speakers just after 14:00 UTC, a 2-year note auction at 17:00 UTC, and UN General Assembly headline flow with live Iran diplomacy and a scheduled Trump-Xi meeting later in the week. Brent has rebounded about 1.3% overnight, partially unwinding the oil relief that powered Monday's advance. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span a strongly directional U.S. session followed by a calm overnight. From 05:00 UTC on 21 September the mode turned trend-up as European and then U.S. buyers extended the advance; Tail rose from 5 to a 33 peak at 19:00 UTC while the Nasdaq-100 ran to a 2.83% record close on AI leadership, falling oil and softer yields. After the 20:00 UTC close volatility decayed quickly, the mode reverted to normal and Tail fell back into the low band, where it has stayed through the Asian session.
outlookSummary: The base case for the next 24 hours is a two-way tape with conditional risk concentrated in the U.S. cash session. Tail is expected to remain in the low band overnight and through Europe, cross the WATCH threshold around the 14:00 UTC Richmond Fed and Fed-speaker cluster and again in the 19:00 UTC closing hour, then fall back after the U.S. close. That path assumes no disorderly front-end move at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and no geopolitical discontinuity out of the UN General Assembly. Escalation beyond the flagged window would require observed one-way structure: shallow or failed retracements with the index holding near session extremes.
